passages.title: The Last Steam Trains
passages.passage:
For more than a century the steam locomotive was the beating heart of the railway, and (1)____ was it more revered than in the small towns whose prosperity depended on the line. Yet by the late 1950s the writing was already (2)____ the wall. Diesel engines, which needed neither a fireman nor hours of preparation before dawn, could be started at the turn of a key, and railway companies, (3)____ accounts had been sliding into the red for years, were quick to see the appeal. No sooner (4)____ the first diesels been delivered than the older engines began to be withdrawn, sometimes with only a few weeks' notice. Crews who had spent thirty years learning to coax a temperamental boiler into life found themselves retrained in a matter of days, and many never (5)____ to terms with the change.

It was the enthusiasts, rather (6)____ the companies, who saved what could be saved. Had they not raised the money to buy engines that were bound (7)____ the scrapyard, hardly a single one would survive today. Instead, several hundred were rescued and restored, and every summer weekend they can still be seen climbing the steep valleys of preserved lines. Not one of them earns a penny in freight, (8)____ they draw far larger crowds than any diesel ever did. What (9)____ them apart, the volunteers insist, is not nostalgia but craft: a steam engine has to be understood, not merely operated. Whether those skills can be handed (10)____ to a generation that has never smelt coal smoke is another question, and one the last of the old drivers ask with some anxiety.

questions.explanation: A negative adverb at the front of a clause forces inversion: nowhere was it more revered than. Never would not fit because the comparison is between places, not times, and there would need normal word order.
The idiom is the writing is on the wall, meaning that an ending is clearly coming. At or against the wall would describe a physical position and lose the idiom.
A possessive relative is needed: the companies' accounts, so whose accounts. Which or that cannot show possession, and their would leave the clause with no relative link.
No sooner had X happened than Y takes the past perfect with subject-auxiliary inversion. Were would give a passive with the wrong tense, and have breaks the past-time sequence.
The collocation is come to terms with something, meaning to accept it. Got or went do not combine with to terms, and the narrative past requires came, not come.
Inside this cleft sentence, rather than contrasts the enthusiasts with the companies. Then is a common misspelling that refers to time, and not cannot follow rather here.
Bound for a place means heading towards it, here the scrapyard. Bound to is followed by a verb (bound to fail), not a destination.

The two halves contrast, so a concessive linker is needed: yet or but (or though/although introducing the second clause). So would make the crowds a result of earning nothing, which is not the meaning.
Set something apart means to make it different or special. Puts and keeps apart would mean physically separating the engines, and the present simple with what requires the -s form.
Skills are handed down (or handed on) to a later generation. Handed over means surrendering something, and handed out means distributing copies.

passages.title: The Map Makers
passages.passage:
Before satellites, a map was only (1)____ good as the people who had walked the ground it showed. Surveyors would set (2)____ at first light with a chain, a compass and a heavy brass instrument for measuring angles, and by nightfall they might have fixed the position of a dozen hills. The work was slow, dangerous and, (3)____ the most part, invisible: nobody thanked a surveyor for a border that ran exactly where it should. So exacting were the standards (4)____ a single error in a baseline measurement could throw out every distance calculated from it for a hundred miles.

It is easy to forget how (5)____ of the world remained blank until quite recently. Well (6)____ the twentieth century, whole river systems appeared on official maps as dotted lines, an honest admission that no one had followed them to their source. The cartographers themselves were rarely the ones who had done the walking; more (7)____ than not, they were drawing up what explorers, traders and soldiers had reported. All too frequently those reports flatly contradicted (8)____ another, and the man at the drawing board had to decide whom to believe. Little (9)____ they know that their careful guesswork would one day be checked from orbit. When that day came, the surprise was not how much they had got wrong (10)____ how much, armed with nothing more than patience and arithmetic, they had got right.

questions.explanation: The equal comparison is only as good as the people. So good as is not used in this positive frame, and too would need a following to-infinitive.
Set off and set out both mean to begin a journey (the older set forth is also possible). Set up means to establish something, and set about would need an object or an -ing form after it.
The fixed phrase is for the most part, meaning mostly. In or on the most part are not English expressions.
The inverted structure So exacting were the standards that... needs that to introduce the result. Which would turn the clause into a relative one with no result meaning.
The world is treated as an uncountable whole, so the quantifier is how much of. Many of requires a plural noun, and most of cannot follow how.
Well into the twentieth century means a long way past its start. Well in is not a time expression, and until would mean the dotted lines stopped exactly then.
The idiom more often than not means usually. Likely gives more likely than not, which describes probability, not frequency of practice, and does not describe what they habitually did.
The reciprocal pronoun is one another (the reports contradicted each other). Each pairs with other, not with another, so each another is impossible.
Little did they know is a fixed inversion in the past simple. Had would require a past participle (had they known), which changes both tense and meaning.
The pattern not X but Y replaces one idea with another. As would need not so much X as Y, and than would need a comparative before it.

passages.title: Why Rivers Bend
passages.passage:
Ask a child to draw a river and the chances (1)____ that it will run straight from the mountains to the sea. Real rivers do nothing (2)____ the kind. Left to themselves, they wander, and the wandering is not random (3)____ all: it obeys rules that engineers have spent a century trying to write down.

The process begins with the smallest irregularity. (4)____ the current meets a patch of softer bank, it eats into it. The water on the outside of the new curve then speeds up, (5)____ the water on the inside slows down and drops the sand it was carrying. The faster water scours the bank (6)____ further, the slower water builds a beach, and so the bend grows. The larger the bend becomes, (7)____ more sharply the river must turn, until eventually the loop is so tight that the water simply breaks through the narrow neck of land and abandons the curve altogether. What is left (8)____ is a crescent-shaped lake, cut off from the stream that made it.

Engineers who straighten rivers in the name of flood control have learned, often at great (9)____, that a river deprived of its bends will spend its energy elsewhere, cutting deeper or flooding faster. Far (10)____ being a flaw, the meander is the river's way of spending its energy safely, and the wiser planners now leave it alone.

questions.explanation: The idiom is the chances are that..., meaning it is likely. Chances is plural, so is fails agreement, and were would clash with the present-tense will run.
Nothing of the kind is a fixed expression meaning not that at all. Like would need nothing like that, and in the kind is not English.
Not ... at all is the emphatic negative. After all means despite expectations, and in all means in total, neither of which fits here.

A conditional or place/time conjunction opens the clause: Where (or when/once/if) the current meets softer bank. Which would need a preceding noun to refer to, and while suggests two simultaneous actions rather than a trigger.

The clause contrasts the outside of the curve with the inside, so while or whereas (or a plain and) fits. But after a comma with this contrast is possible in speech but weak in formal prose, and because would wrongly make one speed the cause of the other.

Still further (or even/yet/ever further) intensifies the comparative and shows the scouring going on beyond its earlier extent; much further is also possible. More further is a double comparative, and very cannot modify a comparative.
Correlative comparatives take the shape the larger ..., the more sharply .... Both halves need the definite article; so or then breaks the pattern.
What remains after the river moves away is left behind. Left over refers to an unused remainder of a quantity, such as food, not to a landform abandoned in place.
At great cost or at great expense means with heavy losses. Price is used with pay a high price, not with at great.
Far from being a flaw denies one description before offering another. Far off and far away describe distance and cannot take an -ing complement in this sense.

passages.title: The Story of the Potato
passages.passage:
Few foods have travelled (1)____ far, or changed as many lives, as the humble potato. Cultivated for thousands of years in the high valleys of the Andes, it reached Europe in the sixteenth century and was, (2)____ first, regarded with deep suspicion. It grew underground, it was not mentioned in any holy book, and it belonged to a family of plants several members of (3)____ were poisonous. For nearly two hundred years it was fed to animals rather (4)____ to people.

Only when famine and war had made grain scarce (5)____ governments begin to promote it in earnest. One king is said to have posted guards around his potato fields by day and quietly withdrawn them by night, (6)____ the assumption that peasants would steal anything worth guarding. (7)____ or not the story is true, the strategy it describes worked: within a generation the crop had taken hold across northern Europe, and a peasant family with a small plot could feed itself through the winter.

The potato's great virtue, that it yields more food per acre than almost any other crop, turned (8)____ to be its great danger as well. Whole regions came to depend on a single variety, so that when disease struck in the 1840s there was nothing to (9)____ back on, and a million people starved. Had those farmers planted the dozens of varieties their Andean predecessors had grown, the blight (10)____ have been no more than a footnote in history rather than a catastrophe.

questions.explanation: The comparison is completed by as the humble potato, so the first half needs as far (or, after the negative-sense few, so far). Too and very cannot pair with a following as.
At first means initially, before attitudes changed. In the first would need a following noun (in the first place), and from first is not idiomatic.
After a preposition in a relative clause only which is possible: several members of which. That cannot follow a preposition, and them would leave two clauses with no link.
Rather than sets one option against another. Then refers to time and is a spelling trap, and instead would need of, not rather.

Only when ... did governments begin: a fronted only phrase forces inversion in the main clause. Had would need a participle, and no inversion at all (governments began) is ungrammatical after Only when.
On the assumption that is the standard collocation. In and with the assumption are not idiomatic, and under collocates with the impression, not the assumption.
Whether or not introduces a concession covering both possibilities. If cannot be followed directly by or not at the start of a sentence, and even would need if after it.
Turn out to be means to prove in the end to be. Turn into takes a noun, not a to-infinitive, and turn up means to arrive.
Fall back on something means to use it as a reserve when the first choice fails. Go back on means to break a promise, and look back on means to remember.

The inverted Had those farmers planted... is a third conditional, so the main clause needs a past modal plus have: might/would/could have been. May is reserved for open possibilities and will cannot look back at an unreal past.

passages.title: The First Hospitals
passages.passage:
Nobody knows exactly when the first hospital opened its doors, partly because the word itself has meant so many different things. In the ancient world, a temple (1)____ the sick would come to pray was, in a sense, a hospital; so was the roadside shelter where a monastery fed and washed travellers. What these places had in (2)____ was charity rather than medicine. A doctor might visit, but the institution existed to (3)____ for the dying, not to cure them.

That began to change in the great cities of the medieval Islamic world, (4)____ rulers competed to endow buildings with wards, pharmacies and libraries. Physicians there kept written records of every patient, an idea (5)____ radical at the time that few outside those cities believed it worth the trouble. Patients were separated (6)____ to their illness, and no one, rich or poor, was turned away.

Europe was slow to catch (7)____. For centuries its hospitals remained crowded, ill-lit places, and a patient who entered one stood a fair chance of leaving it in a coffin. Not (8)____ the nineteenth century, when reformers insisted on clean linen, fresh air and trained nurses, did survival rates begin to climb. Far (9)____ being feared, hospitals came to be trusted, and by the early twentieth century it was in a hospital, not at home, that most people in industrial countries expected to be born.

It is tempting to think of all this as steady progress. In truth, every stage was (10)____ about by someone deciding that the sick deserved better than they were getting.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The clause says the sick came to pray in the temple, so a relative adverb of place is needed: where. Which would need a preposition (to which), and what cannot introduce a relative clause.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Have something in common means to share a feature. In general and in particular are adverbials that cannot take had as their verb, and had in mind would mean intended.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Care for the dying means to look after them. Look for means to search, tend takes a direct object with no for, and attend pairs with to.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The rulers belonged to the cities, so the possessive relative whose rulers is required. Who and whom refer to people directly, and which rulers would make no grammatical link with cities.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Before a bare adjective followed by a that-clause, the intensifier is so: so radical that. Such needs a noun phrase, too is followed by an infinitive, and very cannot introduce a result clause.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: According to their illness means classified by it. Due to, owing to and thanks to all express cause, which is not the meaning of sorting patients into wards.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Catch up means to reach the level others have already reached. Catch on means to become popular or to understand, and catch out means to expose a mistake.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Not until ... did is the fronted negative that triggers the inversion later in the sentence. Before, since and after do not form this structure with not and would leave the inverted did unexplained.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Far from being feared means not feared at all but the opposite. Far off, far away and far apart describe physical distance and cannot govern an -ing clause here.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Bring about means to cause, and the passive was brought about by fits. Come about has the same meaning but is intransitive, so it has no passive, and carried/taken about are not phrasal verbs of causing.
